Reproduced. The page's limits notes say: 'with the elbow held to 120°, 49 of 50 people still managed eating, drinking and washing by moving the shoulder and wrist instead (Vasen 1995), the lowest setting tested.'
The PubMed abstract (fetched; dcv/vasen.txt) says: 'serially limited by 15 degree increments ... 12 activities of daily living ... 49 of the subjects performed all of the tasks with extension limited at 75 degrees and flexion limited at 120 degrees ... compensatory motions and strategies of the normal adjacent joints'.
Three problems:
- The abstract names no tasks, and the fact notes say the full text was not read.
- 'Serially limited by 15 degree increments' means 120° was not the lowest setting tested. It is the tightest setting at which 49 of 50 still managed all tasks, which is the verifier's wording in rec_vasen_120_line.
- The arc was braced at both ends (75-120°).
verdicts.better_fix: In settings.json limits.notes[2]: "A softer line comes earlier. Unaided eating and drinking use about 130 to 136° of elbow bend. With elbow motion braced to 75–120°, 49 of 50 adults still did all 12 daily tasks in the study by using other joints instead (Vasen 1995); that was the tightest brace at which they did, and the abstract does not say how many failed beyond it."

verdicts.reasoning:
Not a defect. The sentence is a measured statement about averages, and the page draws no structural conclusion from it.
ANSUR II male CSV (4,082 men) by height decile:
- BMI is flat: 27.6, 27.5, 27.8, 27.6, 27.9, 27.4, 27.9, 27.7, 27.7, 27.7.
- Weight/H^3 falls steadily from 16.85 to 14.73, about 13% lower in the tallest decile.
Trexler 2017 also finds plain FFMI flat with height (slope 2.943, not significant).
So 'real tall men are slimmer than scaled-up short men, so the score rates them a little lower' is true as a conditional mean. OLS estimates that conditional mean without bias. Burton 2010's dispute is about the structural (latent-size) exponent, not about E[S | height]. The DISPUTED fact's own notes say it 'does not affect' the scaled-copy statement. Whether the cause is structural is not asserted in the ignores line or the score card.
Optional wording only: add 'On average,' at the start.
verdicts.better_fix: None required. Optional: settings.json ignores[0], change 'Real tall men are slimmer' to 'On average, real tall men are slimmer'.
